newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt might postpone economic summit till spring.
newsitem.headline: Egypt might postpone economic summit till spring.

text.p: Egypt might postpone a Middle East economic conference until next spring if negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians do not make enough progress in the next two months, presidential adviser Osama el-Baz said.
"Egypt is not thinking of cancelling the Cairo economic summit but it is studying the right time for holding the summit," Baz told the German-Arab Chamber of Trade on Monday.

"We are consulting with our European, American and Japanese partners to prepare the right atmosphere for holding it, and studying the possibility of postponing it until next spring to give the peace process a chance to progress," he added.
The conference was proposed for Cairo from November 12 to 14. Baz, who is also a senior foreign ministry official, was quoted in the government newspaper al-Ahram on Tuesday.
The adviser said that under present circumstances, without progress in Middle East peace, it would be better to set up an Arab common market than a Middle East market.
"Middle East market" is the diplomatic code for integrating Israel into the economy of the region, the main purpose of the proposed conference.
Egyptian officials have already said that Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron is a minimum condition for the conference taking place on time.
Egypt's ambassador to Israel has named other conditions Israel must meet but Foreign Minister Amr Moussa has declined to confirm these in detail.

Baz said: "The time has not yet come to talk about a Middle East market...The idea of setting up an Arab common market should have priority for us. It will be easier to set up a Middle East market if we have an Arab common market first."
He said Egypt thought Israeli businessmen could try to persuade their government to make progress towards peace "so that regional economic relations rest on sound foundations".
